lead.headline: Kimi Antonelli, 20, becomes Formula One's youngest world champion as Verstappen wins a chaotic Mexico City Grand Prix
lead.byline: FORMULA 1 · AL JAZEERA · THE RACE · 2 NOV
lead.short: Kimi Antonelli finished third in Mexico City on Sunday to win the Formula One drivers' title with four rounds to go, at 20 years and 68 days the youngest champion in the sport's history. Max Verstappen won the red-flagged, restarted race from fifth on the grid, ahead of Lewis Hamilton, after the two Ferrari drivers clashed.

why.text: Mercedes has a champion in his first title fight, and Italy its first since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

more: Antonelli needed only ninth. He kept out of trouble, passed Charles Leclerc at the restart and cried into his helmet after the flag. "On the last lap, I just backed off, because I just couldn't see the track," he said. His lead is now an unassailable 119 points. The previous youngest champion was Sebastian Vettel, at 23 years and 134 days in 2010.

Ferrari ran first and second at Turn 4, but Leclerc was given a five-second penalty for cutting the track in a fight with Hamilton, and Verstappen jumped them both. "When you are 1-2 in Turn 4, you don't imagine that you won't win the race," said team principal Fred Vasseur. George Russell, Antonelli's team-mate, made a poor start, took a 10-second penalty and finished sixth. The race was halted for 33 minutes with 25 of 71 laps left.

update.new: Antonelli is champion; Verstappen won the race.
update.front: A 20-year-old has won the world championship, the youngest in the sport's history.

seconds.headline: The Sensex rises 0.9% to its highest level since September as oil falls and Reliance jumps on its results
seconds.short: The Sensex was up 648 points, or 0.9%, at 75,108 at 2pm, its highest level since 8 September, after jumping more than 900 points in the first hour. Brent crude fell 3.5% to about $109.50 as Iranian and Qatari officials held a third day of talks, and Reliance Industries rose more than 5% after its results.

why.text: India imports most of its oil, so every hope of a deal that reopens Hormuz shows up in share prices and the rupee.

more: The early rally added more than ₹6 lakh crore to the value of BSE-listed companies in under an hour, The Economic Times reported. Tata Steel rose 4%, and NTPC, Maruti Suzuki, BEL, SBI and TCS gained 1% to 3%, while Sun Pharma fell 2%. The Nifty 50 was up 0.9% at 23,260, but the Nifty IT index slipped 0.8% after Friday's 3.5% fall in the Nasdaq-100.

Market breadth was strong, with 2,053 shares rising on the NSE against 921 falling, though small and mid-sized companies gained less than the leaders. Gold recovered to about $3,908 an ounce after a one-year low on Friday, and the rupee held at about 95 a dollar. Investors now look to Tuesday's US midterm elections.

seconds.headline: Rahul Gandhi tells a vast Ramlila Maidan rally that the election chief 'carried out the biggest crime' as 130 million voters were struck off
seconds.byline: THE GUARDIAN · THE NEW INDIAN EXPRESS · 2 NOV
seconds.short: Tens of thousands of opposition supporters filled Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday as the INDIA bloc demanded that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign. Rahul Gandhi said Kumar had "carried out the biggest crime" through a voter-roll revision that has removed 130 million names, and warned Narendra Modi: "You can't run anywhere." The BJP denies the claims.

why.text: It was one of the opposition's largest shows of strength in years, and it sets up a long fight over the voter rolls before the next elections.

more: Gandhi said the alliance would not let "democracy be finished in the country". Congress leaders had predicted that a million people would come. Leaders of the youth-led 'Cockroach' movement, whose summer protests forced a cabinet minister to resign and which marched against the revision last month, backed the rally but did not attend, The Guardian reports.

Jharkhand's health minister, Irfan Ansari, told the crowd he had brought 10,000 people and would take Kumar to Ranchi if he did not resign, and warned of unrest like that in Bangladesh or Nepal. The opposition says the revision of the rolls helps the BJP; the party says the rally was staged to spread disorder in Delhi during the festive season.

facts.Ansari: threatened to take Kumar to Ranchi

update.new: The rally took place: tens of thousands, and Gandhi's charge of 'the biggest crime'.
update.front: The opposition's biggest rally in years has made the voter-roll fight a national confrontation.

seconds.headline: Alcaraz beats de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win the Vienna title for the first time
seconds.short: Carlos Alcaraz beat Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 in 1 hour and 27 minutes on Sunday to win the Erste Bank Open in Vienna for the first time. The second seed, who entered as a wildcard, said he had stopped complaining about the slow, heavy balls he has long disliked, and credited a serve he rebuilt at home after Shanghai.

why.text: It is his last title before the Paris Masters and the ATP Finals, and he goes into both on a winning run.

more: "This week I just tried to accept it as it is, with this ball," Alcaraz said. "I tried to be positive, I tried not to think about it too much and just keep going." He said he had worked on the directions and speed of his serve, above all the second serve, and won a high share of the points behind his first serve all week.

De Minaur, who had beaten top seed Alexander Zverev in the semi-finals, said Alcaraz was much harder to rush than when he beat him in the 2025 Rotterdam final. "In these conditions he's able to absorb the pace really well and still be able to redirect his shots," he said. Alcaraz leads their head-to-head 7-0, and plays his first Paris match in the second round on Wednesday.

update.front: Alcaraz has won a title on the eve of the year's last Masters event.

seconds.headline: Americans vote on Tuesday for control of Congress, as a Michigan Democrat backs her party's Republican rival and a judge throws out a Trump-backed suit in Alaska
seconds.short: The US votes in midterm elections on Tuesday, with control of Congress at stake. In Michigan, Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, on Sunday. In Alaska, a judge dismissed a Justice Department suit to block certification of the Senate result if Republican Dan Sullivan loses.

why.text: The result decides how free a hand Donald Trump has for his last two years, on tariffs and on the war with Iran, both of which reach India.

more: Stevens's endorsement followed a feud with El-Sayed over Israel. Michigan's Democratic chair, Curtis Hertel, condemned it, and her chief of staff of eight years, Justin German, and her communications director quit and backed El-Sayed. Bernie Sanders also attacked her.

Trump said on 23 October he had ordered the Alaska suit. The Justice Department argued that two candidates named Dan Sullivan on the ballot could confuse voters; a New York Times investigation found that aides to the Democrat, Mary Peltola, recruited the second man, which she says she knew nothing about. The department says it will appeal, and Sullivan told CNN he would accept the result. Senator Chris Murphy of Connecticut has had a stroke and is expected to recover, the BBC reports.

stories.headline: Delhi's air turns 'very poor' for the first time this season, a day after its winter curbs began
stories.short: Delhi's Air Quality Index reached 312 at 9am on Monday, in the 'very poor' band for the first time this season, a day after the city's winter pollution curbs took effect. More smog is expected in the coming days. The Congress's Jairam Ramesh said India's PM2.5 limits are four times the WHO's 24-hour guideline and must be revised.

why.text: Very poor air brings in the second stage of the city's emergency plan, and the season's worst weeks are still ahead.

more: The Central Pollution Control Board rates an AQI of 301 to 400 as very poor and anything above 400 as severe. Stage 2 of the Graded Response Action Plan applies when the index enters the very poor band. The curbs that began on Sunday ban outdoor construction and older vehicles registered outside Delhi, and require offices to keep half their staff at home.

Ramesh said the National Clean Air Programme concentrates on PM10, while the finer PM2.5 is the real danger to health, and that India's annual PM2.5 standard is eight times the WHO's. "The PM2.5 standards need to be revised urgently and enforced strictly," he said, taking a dig at what he called the "so-called PM 3.0 government".

facts.band: very poor, first time this season

update.new: The AQI crossed 300 a day after the curbs began.

stories.headline: Anthropic stops Claude from building recreations of existing video games, and some developers say original projects are blocked too
stories.short: Anthropic has updated Claude so it will no longer build recreations of specific existing video games, while still helping with original games, genre games and games from users' own designs. Addy Osmani of Anthropic's technical staff confirmed the change, saying using Claude to infringe IP breaks its usage policy. Some developers say legitimate projects are being blocked.

why.text: Coding agents can now copy a whole game quickly, and where AI companies draw the line on IP shapes what developers can build with them.

more: The new instruction, first spotted by a user on X, reads: "Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user's own designs and assets. Do not build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original." Osmani said Anthropic would "continue to iterate to ensure we're striking the right balance".

The change follows a wave of big games decompiled with AI help and put online to play in browsers, including Halo: Combat Evolved, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 and Grand Theft Auto V. Last year Anthropic agreed to a record $1.5bn settlement with authors who said it trained its models on their books, and the estate of Elvis Presley has since sued it.

facts.rule: no recreations of specific existing games

briefs.headline: NASA's Swift telescope will fall back to Earth in the next few days, after a rescue mission failed to lift its orbit
briefs.text: The 1,500 kg observatory, launched in 2004 to study gamma-ray bursts, will re-enter uncontrolled, and where it falls is not yet known. Its orbit had decayed to 275 km by 20 October.

briefs.headline: Four volunteers emerge from NASA's 378-day simulated Mars mission in Houston
briefs.text: They lived in a 158-square-metre 3D-printed habitat at the Johnson Space Center from 19 October 2025, growing crops and talking to Earth with built-in delays. NASA hopes to send people to Mars as early as the 2030s.

briefs.headline: Arsenal win 1-0 at Anfield through Kai Havertz, with Declan Rice praised for a defensive masterclass
briefs.text: Havertz scored the only goal, and Jamie Carragher called Rice "world class" after Arsenal held on. Liverpool's best chance of a way back, a penalty claim for Jurrien Timber's pull on Alexander Isak's shirt, was turned down.

briefs.headline: Liverpool's Andoni Iraola says he will tell his players to dive after a penalty is refused against Arsenal
briefs.text: Isak stayed on his feet when Timber grabbed his shirt, and VAR's Stuart Attwell let the decision stand. "The answer is you have to dive, if you don't dive they won't call it," Iraola said.

update.new: Liverpool lost to Arsenal; Iraola's dive remarks.

stories.headline: Real Madrid win 3-0 at Racing Santander for a sixth straight victory, with goals from Mbappé, Bellingham and Diomande
stories.short: Real Madrid beat Racing Santander 3-0 on Sunday for their sixth win in a row. Kylian Mbappé opened the scoring from the penalty spot, Jude Bellingham finished a well-timed run for the second, and Yan Diomande added a spectacular third. Thibaut Courtois made one outstanding save to keep the clean sheet.

why.text: Madrid travel to AEK Athens in the Champions League on Wednesday on a run of six straight wins.

more: Arda Güler created six key passes, five of them in the first half, provided an assist and completed 97.5% of his passes, Managing Madrid's ratings note. Dean Huijsen played the pass out of Racing's press that started Bellingham's goal, and made seven clearances and four blocked shots. Marc Cucurella shut down his flank with four tackles and four interceptions.

Trent Alexander-Arnold, who had fallen to third choice at right-back, started and gave Bellingham, Güler and Mbappé an outlet on the right. Aurélien Tchouaméni made six interceptions. Chinese state television is still not showing Madrid's matches after the row over a meme involving Mbappé and Mao, Al Jazeera reports. Madrid play at Valencia on Saturday.

briefs.headline: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg scores 37, the most by a Golden State rookie since Stephen Curry in 2010
briefs.text: With Curry resting his knee, the 24-year-old led a 124-112 win over the Los Angeles Clippers, the Warriors' fourth in a row. Curry's 42 in 2010 is the only higher total by a Warriors rookie.

briefs.text: The unseeded Monegasque beat eighth seed Jiri Lehecka 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 on Sunday, a year after winning in Shanghai, and returns to the top 30. He plays Djokovic in the Paris first round.
